headline: Key stocks to watch include TCS, Trent, Sun Pharma, Tata Steel, M&M, and HDFC Bank.
hook: Six stocks dominate Monday's trading radar
summary: Ahead of the trading session on Monday, October 12, major corporate announcements and share price triggers put TCS, Trent, Sun Pharma, Tata Steel, Mahindra & Mahindra, and HDFC Bank in focus. Investors and traders are monitoring these prominent names for corporate developments and earnings cues. These companies span key sectors including IT, retail, pharma, metals, auto, and banking, driving overall market sentiment. why_it_matters: Index heavyweight movements could drive overall market direction today.

headline: PERM labor certification requests decline for major Indian IT firms
hook: US visa filings drop for Indian IT
summary: Data shows a notable decline in PERM labor certification requests submitted by top Indian IT service providers including TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. PERM certification is a critical first step for companies seeking to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency in the United States. The reduction reflects shifting hiring strategies, localized recruitment efforts, or immigration processing trends in the US market. Indian retail investors tracking major tech exporters must monitor how this impacts onsite staffing costs and talent management.
why_it_matters: Higher local hiring costs could squeeze tech exporters' margins.
winners_losers: US local tech workers gain / Indian IT firms hurt

headline: TCS skips quarterly variable pay for senior staff while juniors get full payouts
hook: Senior pay withheld amid rising AI revenues
summary: Tata Consultancy Services has withheld quarterly variable pay for senior employees of grade C3A and above due to missed internal performance targets. Meanwhile, junior staff will receive their full eligible payouts. This internal compensation adjustment occurs as the company reports nearly 20 percent growth in AI revenue. Retail investors can track how workforce cost structures align with shifting technology revenue models.
why_it_matters: Senior cost controls at TCS reflect shifting tech revenue priorities.
winners_losers: Junior employees gain / senior employees hurt

This recovery occurred despite mid-week market pressure caused by the RBI's decision to hike interest rates. The index's resilience signals a shift in sentiment for large-cap equities.

Investors are interpreting the results as an early signal of a demand recovery in the technology sector. whats_next: Upcoming quarterly results from other major IT firms

headline: US green card freeze sees TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCLTech secure only 61 certified PERM cases in FY26
hook: PERM approvals drop sharply for IT majors
summary: Major Indian IT services firms TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCLTech recorded a combined total of just 61 certified PERM cases in fiscal year 2026 due to a US green card freeze. The PERM labor certification is a crucial first step for employers seeking to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency in the United States. This severe restriction highlights the ongoing challenges Indian IT companies face regarding US visa policies and foreign talent retention. Indian retail investors holding shares in these IT majors should monitor escalating operational hurdles in their primary overseas market.
whats_next: US immigration policy updates regarding employment-based green cards
why_it_matters: US visa constraints threaten talent retention for top Indian IT exporters.
winners_losers: US domestic tech workers gain / Indian IT firms hurt

headline: TCS senior management to skip variable pay for Q2
hook: TCS senior staff denied quarterly variable pay
summary: Tata Consultancy Services has informed senior employees that they will not receive variable pay for the September quarter. The decision follows a broader trend of cost-optimization within the IT sector. This move affects only the senior leadership tier, while junior and mid-level staff remain unaffected. For retail investors, this signals a continued focus on margin protection amid a challenging global demand environment for IT services.
why_it_matters: Signals margin pressure and cost-cutting focus in major IT firms.
winners_losers: TCS margins gain / Senior employees hurt

headline: Donald Trump signals potential restrictions on H-1B tech visas
hook: Trump targets H-1B visa program reforms
summary: Former President Donald Trump has indicated plans to tighten or restrict the H-1B visa program if re-elected. The program is a primary pathway for Indian IT professionals to work in the United States. Changes could include stricter eligibility criteria or caps, potentially disrupting the talent pipeline for major Indian software services firms. This shift creates uncertainty for companies heavily reliant on deploying Indian engineers to US client sites.
why_it_matters: Higher operational costs for Indian IT firms servicing US clients.
winners_losers: US domestic tech talent gains / Indian IT hurt
